title: Minestrone
subtitle: Italian vegetable and bean soup with pasta
excerpt: Italy's great vegetable soup: a thick, deeply flavoured pot of seasonal vegetables, cannellini beans, and small pasta cooked in a rich tomato-based broth. Endlessly adaptable, truly nourishing, and better the day after it is made.

recipe.sourceNotes: Minestrone (from the Italian minestra, meaning soup, with the augmentative suffix -one suggesting a big, substantial soup) is one of the oldest Italian dishes, with written references dating to the Roman period. It is not a fixed recipe but a method and a philosophy: whatever vegetables are in season, cooked slowly in a good broth with beans and pasta or rice. Regional variations across Italy are vast; Genoese versions contain pesto stirred in at the end, Milanese versions often include rice, and Tuscan versions omit pasta entirely. The defining characteristics are the slow initial soffritto (the gently cooked base of onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil), the use of dried beans, and the long, gentle simmer that makes the vegetables meltingly soft and the broth thick and rich.

content.text: Start with a long, patient soffritto: the onion, carrot, and celery should cook in olive oil for at least 15 minutes until completely soft, sweet, and beginning to caramelise. This is the flavour base everything else builds on. Add the pasta in the last 10 minutes only; pasta added too early absorbs all the broth and turns soft.

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a very large pot. Cook the onion, carrot, and celery over low-medium heat for 15 minutes until completely soft. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the potato, courgette, tinned tomatoes, stock, bay leaves, thyme, and parmesan rind. Season. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes. Add the cannellini beans and cavolo nero. Cook for a further 10 minutes.

Add the pasta and cook for the time given on the packet, usually 8 to 10 minutes, until just tender. Remove the bay leaves and parmesan rind. Taste and adjust the salt. Serve in deep bowls with grated parmesan and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.
